# Smritium

> Smritium is the sovereign memory layer for AI: a local-first, privacy-preserving
> memory substrate that captures documents, notes, mail, and calendar and turns them
> into cited, verifiable recall. The entire memory loop — capture, embedding,
> retrieval, reasoning — runs on the user's machine. Cloud models are optional,
> swappable accelerators, never dependencies. From Sanskrit smṛti (स्मृति),
> "that which is remembered." Built by DataFrontier Innovations Pvt Ltd (Bengaluru,
> India) with support from the ELEVATE Nxt programme, Government of Karnataka.

Key facts:
- Local-first by construction: embeddings computed on-device (sentence-transformers),
  vectors in LanceDB on disk, metadata in local SQLite. Zero corpus bytes required
  to leave the device.
- Verifiable memory: content-addressed chunks; deterministic chunking means an
  independent re-ingest reproduces 100% of chunk hashes; every answer cites its
  source chunk IDs; low-confidence abstention instead of fabricated citations.
- Context Rehydrator: retrieval fuses semantic, temporal, and relational signals
  into one ranked context window.
- Consent-gated ambient capture: filesystem/mail/calendar events route through an
  approval inbox before entering durable memory.
- Graceful degradation: works fully offline; pluggable inference (Ollama local,
  optional remote, mock).
- Enterprise "Membrane": PII redaction, approval-gated egress, tamper-evident
  egress audit log — for regulated buyers (legal, finance, healthcare, government).
- MCP bridge (coming soon): smritium_search, smritium_ask, smritium_list_sources —
  agents get cited, approval-scoped answers; the corpus never leaves the device.
- Pricing: free open core; Pro $15/mo (multi-device LAN/P2P sync, connectors,
  Cmd+K overlay, MCP bridge); Enterprise custom (Membrane, on-prem, compliance).
